name: Ahlai
overview: Ahlai is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Zabad, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 11:41. There is no information about his tribal affiliation or additional notes that provide further context about his life or role in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahlai is a proper name meaning 'Alas! I wish that!'. This meaning is directly associated with the Hebrew origin of the name as presented in 1 Chronicles 11:41. There are no titles or additional names linked to him in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Ahlai as the father of Zabad, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections or relationships are recorded in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Ahlai's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his role as the progenitor of Zabad, a figure mentioned in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles 11:41. While details about Ahlai himself are sparse, his mention contributes to the lineage and historical context of those associated with King David's warriors. His inclusion in the genealogical record underscores the importance of family heritage in the biblical account.
